BIIB.note: Closed at a new 52-week high after a 27% rise in 3 months, yet still only 16x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.54 and a 1-year Sharpe of 1.51.
BIIB.bull: Earnings are expected to grow about 30% next year (EPS 12.53 to 16.26), which is why the PEG is so low, and gains over the past year have come with only moderate swings (31% annualised volatility).
BIIB.bear: It is sitting at its 52-week high and the average analyst target is only 3% above today's price. Next-year EPS estimates slipped 2% over 90 days, with revisions split 12 up and 12 down.
BIIB.catalyst: Reported Oct 28; the next report is not yet scheduled. Watch for estimate revisions turning positive.

HUM.note: Up 17% in 3 months and 74% in a year, at a new 52-week high after reporting on Nov 6. EPS is forecast to nearly double next year, which gives the lowest PEG on the shortlist (0.29) despite a 25x forward P/E.
HUM.bull: Analysts are moving one way: 7 upward EPS revisions and none down in 30 days, next-year estimates up 4% in 90 days, and an average target 8% above today's price.
HUM.bear: The low PEG depends on EPS recovering from 9.24 to about 17.19, which rests on Medicare Advantage margins. The stock has more than doubled from its 52-week low of 164, so a disappointment could hit hard.
HUM.catalyst: Medicare Advantage open enrollment runs to Dec 7; enrollment and 2027 guidance updates follow.

MET.note: Within 1% of its 52-week high, up 6% in 3 months, and the cheapest of the three picks at 9.2x forward earnings with a PEG of 1.0.
MET.bull: Low volatility (24% annualised) with a 1-year Sharpe of 1.21. Analysts raised next-year estimates 7 times and cut once in 30 days, and the average target is 6% above today's price.
MET.bear: Expected EPS growth is modest at about 9%, so this is a steady compounder rather than a fast grower. Insurers are sensitive to interest rates and credit markets.
MET.catalyst: Reported Nov 4; the next report is expected in early February.
